name: The Chosen People / doctrine of election
plain_explanation: The belief that God has picked out one group of people for special love and a special destiny, even though they may suffer greatly in the present.
precise_definition: The doctrine that a small section of mankind is specially loved and chosen by God; for the Jews this was the nation of Israel, for Christians it became 'the elect.'
why_it_mattered: It let a small, frequently defeated nation retain a sense of unique importance and purpose, and it supplied Christianity with its own doctrine of an elect community destined for salvation.
historical_origin: Rooted in early tribal religion but sharpened into an exclusive doctrine during and after the Babylonian exile, alongside the new insistence on ritual and legal separateness.
examples: Israel as Yahweh's chosen nation despite conquest and exile
The Christian doctrine of 'the elect' predestined to salvation
influence_on_later_thinkers: Carried directly into Christian theology (discussed further in Chapters II and IV), where the Church replaces the Jewish nation as the community of the elect.
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Underpinned Jewish national pride under foreign domination and, later, underpinned Christian claims to exclusive religious truth.

evolution.treatment: The belief that God has picked out one group of people for special love and a special destiny, even though they may suffer greatly in the present.
